info.title: Perplexity Orchestrator API (OpenAI Responses-compatible)
info.description: OpenAI Responses-compatible access to models across providers. Schema structure is derived from the Apache-2.0-licensed OpenResponses specification and documents the Orchestrator API's supported request and response shapes.

post.description: Generate a model response using the OpenAI Responses schema. Set `stream: true` to receive typed server-sent events followed by `data: [DONE]`.

200.description: Successful response. JSON for non-streaming requests; a `text/event-stream` of typed response events when `stream` is true.

400.description: Invalid request — malformed body, unsupported parameter, or a model that is not available on the Orchestrator API.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded or the selected model is overloaded. Retry after the `Retry-After` interval.

500.description: The request could not be completed because of a server error.

model.description: The model that will process the request, as a `creator/model-name` id from the Orchestrator API catalog.

input.description: Context to provide to the model for the scope of this request. May either be a string or an array of input items. If a string is provided, it is interpreted as a user message.

tools.description: A list of tools that the model may call while generating the response.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature to use, between 0 and 2. Higher values make the output more random.

top_p.description: Nucleus sampling parameter, between 0 and 1. The model considers only the tokens with the top cumulative probability.

parallel_tool_calls.description: Whether the model may call multiple tools in parallel.

stream.description: Whether to stream response events as server-sent events.

max_output_tokens.description: The maximum number of tokens the model may generate for this response.

safety_identifier.description: A stable identifier used for safety monitoring and abuse detection.

prompt_cache_key.description: A key to use when reading from or writing to the prompt cache.

instructions.description: Additional instructions to guide the model for this request.

id.description: The unique ID of the response that was created.

object.description: The object type, which was always `response`.

created_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the response was created.

completed_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the response was completed, if it was completed.

status.description: The status that was set for the response.

incomplete_details.description: Details about why the response was incomplete, if applicable.

model.description: The model that generated this response.

previous_response_id.description: The ID of the previous response in the chain that was referenced, if any.

instructions.description: Additional instructions that were used to guide the model for this response.

output.description: The output items that were generated by the model.

error.description: The error that occurred, if the response failed.

tools.description: The tools that were available to the model during response generation.

parallel_tool_calls.description: Whether the model was allowed to call multiple tools in parallel.

text.description: The text output configuration used for this response.

top_p.description: The nucleus sampling parameter that was used for this response.

presence_penalty.description: The presence penalty that was used to penalize new tokens based on whether they appear in the text so far.

frequency_penalty.description: The frequency penalty that was used to penalize new tokens based on their frequency in the text so far.

top_logprobs.description: The number of most likely tokens that were returned at each position, along with their log probabilities.

temperature.description: The sampling temperature that was used for this response.

reasoning.description: The reasoning configuration used for this response.

usage.description: Token usage statistics that were recorded for the response, if available.

max_output_tokens.description: The maximum number of tokens the model was allowed to generate for this response.

max_tool_calls.description: The maximum number of tool calls the model was allowed to make while generating the response.

store.description: Whether this response was stored so it can be retrieved later.

background.description: Whether this request was run in the background.

service_tier.description: The service tier that was used for this response.

metadata.description: Developer-defined metadata associated with the response.

safety_identifier.description: A stable identifier that was used for safety monitoring and abuse detection.

prompt_cache_key.description: A key that was used to read from or write to the prompt cache.

ToolChoiceParam.description: Controls which tool the model should use, if any.

MetadataParam.description:
Set of 16 key-value pairs that can be attached to an object. This can be         useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured         format, and querying for objects via API or the dashboard.
        Keys are strings with a maximum length of 64 characters. Values are strings         with a maximum length of 512 characters.

effort.description: Controls the level of reasoning effort the model should apply. Higher effort may increase latency and cost.

ReasoningParam.description: **gpt-5 and o-series models only** Configuration options for [reasoning models](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/reasoning).

x-enumDescriptions.auto: Choose a service tier automatically based on current account state.

A description of what the response format is for, used by the model to
determine how to respond in the format.

name.description:
The name of the response format. Must be a-z, A-Z, 0-9, or contain
underscores and dashes, with a maximum length of 64.

schema.title: JSON schema
schema.description: The schema for the response format, described as a JSON Schema object.

strict.description:
Whether to enable strict schema adherence when generating the output.
If set to true, the model will always follow the exact schema defined
in the `schema` field. Only a subset of JSON Schema is supported when
`strict` is `true`.
